messages.author: aa27f7883a8a117c
messages.subject: Peak picking and alignment
parts:
Hello,

Thanks for the great package! 

I would like to know if it is possible to perform peak picking (using "peakPick") for all spectra and then extract a list of mz values (at which peaks occur) for each spectrum (or each pixel) individually without doing alignment. I would also appreciate it if you just write me  a simple illustration of how to use known peaks in spectra for alignment using "peakAlign" i.e. aligning using a set of known peaks. 

Thanks 

Denis

messages.author: 5276ff4387de2618
messages.subject: Re: Peak picking and alignment
parts:
Hi Denis,

You can get a list of all the peaks' m/z values and intensities for each pixel from a peak-picked dataset by doing:

pData(mzData(imageData(object))) # list of m/z values of peaks at each pixel
pData(peakData(imageData(object))) # list of intensities of peaks at each pixel

To use known peaks, just create a vector of the known m/z values for the peaks, and use it for the 'ref' parameter in peakAlign, e.g.:

mypeaks <- c(187, 535, 2000, 4363, 5000) # m/z values of known peaks
mydataset2 <- peakAlign(mydataset, ref=mypeaks)

(When there is no 'ref', Cardinal just creates it automatically from the local maxima of the mean spectrum.)

Hope this helps!

-Kyle

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Peak picking and alignment
parts:
Hi Denis,

The peakAlign method only does alignment of individual peaks to a reference, not spectral alignment (which aligns the whole spectrum).

The default is to compare the m/z of each peak to peaks in the reference and match them either by their difference in ppm or m/z units. Another method using dynamic programming is also available. (The default reference, if none if given, is the local maxima in the mean spectrum.)

Full spectral alignment isn't currently implemented in Cardinal. If there is a particular method you'd like to see implemented for it, please send me a paper reference which describes the method.

-Kylie

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Peak picking and alignment
parts:
That is correct.

The peakPick method only detects peaks, but does not reduce the dataset. The full spectra are still stored, as the "iData" element of the imageData slot. The intensities of the unaligned peaks are stored as a sparse matrix in the "peakData" element of the imageData slot, and their m/z values are likewise stored in the "mzData" element.

After peakAlign, only the peaks matched to the reference are retained. The "iData" element of imageData will consist of only the aligned peaks, and the "peakData" and "mzData" elements will be dropped.

-Kylie
